task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-028 is genuinely done before it's allowed to be marked so. Do not trust TEST-RUNNER's report alone -- re-run the suite yourself. Confirm every acceptance criterion against actual code/tests. Note: working tree has unrelated pre-existing uncommitted files -- do not touch them.
acceptance_criteria: a graph satisfying all 8 checks returns {valid: true, violations: []}
each of the 8 named checks (CHK-01 through CHK-08) has at least one explicit failing-example test demonstrating its specific violation code is returned, not just a generic invalid-graph test
a graph violating 3 of the 8 checks simultaneously returns all 3 violations in one call, not just the first encountered (Key invariant 5)

a cycle that passes through an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY or PARALLEL_GATEWAY node is explicitly permitted (not flagged as CYCLE_WITHOUT_GATEWAY), and a self-loop is explicitly rejected, each with its own test
the function signature and its call sites confirm zero Repo/database calls anywhere in its call graph

result.summary: Independently re-ran `mix test` (full suite) myself, not trusting TEST-RUNNER's report: `Result: 161 passed (4 properties, 157 tests)`, exit code 0, matching the prior report exactly (161 passed/157 tests/4 properties, 0 failures, 0 excluded). Ran `test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs` in isolation too: 15/15 pass. All 5 acceptance criteria checked against actual code (lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex) and tests (test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs), not against prior handoff summaries: (1) 'valid graph -> {valid:true,violations:[]}' -- validate_graph/1's body concatenates 8 check functions via Enum.flat_map and sets valid: violations == [] by construction (line 151); test at graph_test.exs:67-89 exercises a realistic multi-node graph including a permitted gateway cycle and asserts the exact map. (2) 'each of CHK-01..CHK-08 has an explicit failing-example test for its own code' -- confirmed 8 dedicated describe blocks (lines 97-278) covering :missing_start_node, :multiple_start_nodes, :missing_end_node, :dangling_edge, :isolated_node, :duplicate_node_id, :cycle_without_gateway, :node_limit_exceeded, :edge_limit_exceeded -- all 9 violation codes across the 8 named checks are exercised by name-specific fixtures, not a generic invalid-graph test. (3) '3 simultaneous violations in one call' -- graph_test.exs:284-311 constructs a graph with no START, no END, and a non-gateway 2-node cycle, asserts codes(result) == [:missing_start_node, :missing_end_node, :cycle_without_gateway] in fixed order, length 3; matches validate_graph/1's flat_map-over-ordered-check-list implementation which never short-circuits. (4) gateway-cycle-permitted + self-loop-rejected -- graph_test.exs:318-370 has 3 tests: a PARALLEL_GATEWAY cycle returns fully valid (not just 'doesn't also trip another check'), a self-loop on a non-gateway HUMAN_TASK returns :cycle_without_gateway, and a self-loop ON an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY node returns fully valid -- each with its own dedicated test as required. (5) zero Repo/DB calls -- grepped lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex for 'Repo.': zero matches; grepped lib/ for other modules referencing Letflow.Definitions.Graph: zero matches (nothing calls it yet, so its own call graph is the entire surface, and it is pure Enum/Map/MapSet/Kernel throughout, confirmed by reading the full 453-line file). Staleness check: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-028 status is 'in_progress' (line 1198) and docs/status/requirement_status.yaml has exactly one REQ-028 event ('started', 2026-08-16T10:50:50Z, line 1728) and no 'done' event -- consistent, not stale. No docs/migration/decisions/ record references the graph validator (checked all 4 decision files), so nothing shipped contradicts one. This is a WF-02 run, not a WF-04 stage-gate, so no stage-doc REVIEWER sign-off section applies here. Empirical spot-check (own fixtures, not copied from the test file): (a) built a graph with two disjoint components -- a valid START->HUMAN_TASK->END chain plus an isolated SERVICE_TASK with a self-loop on itself -- hand-derived the expected result as exactly one :cycle_without_gateway violation naming the self-loop node before running, then ran it via `mix run` against the real module: exact match, confirming CHK-06 visits every node index including ones in disconnected islands, not just nodes reachable from START. (b) Independently assessed the CHK-05 'duplicate-node-id-never-fires-alone' structural claim (the design's one deliberate deviation from a naive reading) by reading build_node_index/1 (Map.put_new -- first occurrence wins) and check_isolated_nodes/1 (incoming/outgoing sets populated only via node_index lookups on edge.source/edge.target) together: since node_index only ever maps a duplicated id string to its FIRST occurrence's position, a later-occurrence node's own list-position index can never appear in either the outgoing or incoming MapSet, regardless of what edges exist or what node_type it has -- so isolated_node's `cond` always evaluates true for that node (START needs outgoing, END needs incoming, everything else needs both, and it has neither). This means CHK-05 provably cannot fire without a co-occurring CHK-04 :isolated_node violation for that same node. Verified this proof empirically too with a second fresh fixture NOT in the test file (duplicate id on an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, with edges that legitimately connect the first occurrence) via `mix run`: got exactly [:duplicate_node_id, :isolated_node], matching the hand-derivation. The claim holds.
